name: Graph Edit Distance and Maximum Common Subgraph
problem_statement: Given two graphs, compute either the minimum total cost of vertex/edge insertions, deletions, and substitutions transforming one graph into the other (graph edit distance), or a largest common induced or non-induced subgraph shared by both (maximum common subgraph).

normalization: Both graphs in the pair must use the same direction and label semantics.
Remove self-loops unless the cost/isomorphism definition explicitly covers them.
Collapse parallel edges per the declared multigraph policy; default is to reject multi-edges.

problem_inputs.name: task
problem_inputs.description: Compute minimum edit cost or a largest common subgraph.

problem_inputs.name: induced
problem_inputs.description: For maximum_common_subgraph, whether the common subgraph must be vertex-induced in both graphs.

problem_inputs.name: edit_costs
problem_inputs.description: Per-operation nonnegative costs used when task=graph_edit_distance.

problem_inputs.name: label_match_policy
problem_inputs.description: How vertex/edge labels affect substitution cost or common-subgraph eligibility.

problem_inputs.name: time_budget_seconds
problem_inputs.description: Optional wall-clock budget after which the best proven bound and incumbent solution are returned.

problem_inputs.name: solution_quality
problem_inputs.description: Whether a heuristic/approximate result with a disclosed bound is permitted.

required_outputs.name: task_result
required_outputs.description: distance (number) for graph_edit_distance, or subgraph (vertex/edge sets with the correspondence mapping) for maximum_common_subgraph.

required_outputs.name: optimal
required_outputs.description: Whether global optimality was proven within any stated time_budget_seconds.

optional_outputs.name: vertex_correspondence
optional_outputs.description: Mapping between the two graphs' vertices realizing the returned edit path or common subgraph; null marks an inserted/deleted vertex.

optional_outputs.name: edit_path
optional_outputs.description: Ordered list of edit operations realizing graph_edit_distance.

optional_outputs.name: lower_bound
optional_outputs.description: Best proven bound when optimal=false due to a time budget.

optional_outputs.name: approximation_bound
optional_outputs.description: Certified gap for an approximate result.

solution_semantics.objective: Minimize total edit_costs over a sequence of operations transforming graph A into graph B (graph_edit_distance), or maximize the vertex count of a common subgraph consistent with label_match_policy and induced (maximum_common_subgraph).
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact mode requires optimal=true; approximate/time-budgeted mode must disclose lower_bound or approximation_bound.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Multiple optimal correspondences may exist; return one unless alternates are explicitly requested.
solution_semantics.ordering: edit_path, when returned, is ordered as an applicable operation sequence; vertex_correspondence is an unordered mapping.

validation_rules: Applying edit_path to graph A reproduces graph B exactly.
task_result.distance equals the sum of edit_costs over edit_path.
vertex_correspondence for maximum_common_subgraph is injective and every mapped edge exists in both graphs (and, if induced=true, non-edges correspond to non-edges).
Reported optimal=true matches independent verification against an exhaustive oracle on small fixtures.
edge_cases: Identical graphs have graph_edit_distance zero and maximum_common_subgraph equal to the whole graph.
Disjoint label alphabets with label_match_policy=exact force every vertex substitution to use insertion+deletion cost.
One or both input graphs empty is a valid degenerate case with a well-defined distance or empty common subgraph.
A time_budget_seconds expiring before proof of optimality must still return a feasible incumbent with optimal=false.

correctness: distance or subgraph-size agreement with exact oracle on small fixtures
